A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAD/MAD2R research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendix A. Reordered proofs and relocated displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on nine datasets, parameter-sensitivity studies and the synthetic example in Section 6.2.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds original frequency, user-coverage and entry-coverage results for Reddit and Common Crawl.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same thresholding, adaptive weighting, rerouting, biasing and two-round procedures. Their relocation and explanatory edits do not change the methods. Appendix A's Basic algorithm is identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine datasets in Table 1 and the same synthetic heavy/light-item scenario in Section 6.2. The additional coverage analysis reuses Reddit and Common Crawl.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Basic, DP-SIPS, PolicyGaussian and GreedyUpdate with the same participation across datasets. The parameter sweeps and synthetic example also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The added absolute-utility evaluation uses delta = 10^-11 for Common Crawl, alongside the retained Table 2 comparison at delta = 10^-5. It introduces frequency-bucket coverage and percentages of users and entries represented by returned items. Existing benchmark and sensitivity-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 1 and the Absolute Utility discussion examine which item frequencies are recovered and how broadly outputs cover users and entries on two retained datasets. The four existing parameter-sensitivity studies and synthetic example remain.

E5.justification: Both Table 2 captions specify five trials and one standard deviation for smaller datasets. V2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance procedures for the new analysis.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Clueweb MAD2R output from 36,073,952 to 34,533,524 under unchanged stated settings, making DP-SIPS's 34,889,208 the best parallel result. Other Table 2 entries remain unchanged. Additional utility results include 16,551,550 Common Crawl items at delta = 10^-11 and user/entry coverage percentages for both analyzed datasets.

T1.justification: The formal privacy and utility guarantees, assumptions and derivations are retained. Theorem 3.3's proof moves to Section 5.1, sensitivity lemmas are reordered, and the existing technical lemma moves to Section 5.3; these are organizational changes.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract's 'across the board' wording and the introduction's claim of winning on every dataset. Section 7.4 now reports MAD2R winning seven rather than eight of nine parallel comparisons. The method, privacy and scalability contributions remain, although some blanket performance claims persist.

C2.justification: V2 interprets low distinct-item recovery alongside high user/entry coverage and many rare items. It identifies Clueweb as an exception associated with unusual dataset statistics. The new conclusion explicitly discusses the remaining sequential-performance gap and the absence of quantitative guarantees against a defined optimum.

D1.justification: Section 7.3 adds a repository link for an open-source Python implementation; v1 described implementation languages without providing this access information. Existing hardware, computational framework and runtime descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 1.3 retains the positioning against uniform weighting, sequential greedy approaches and DP-SIPS. Removed repeated citations and changed reference back-links do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 edits introductory prose, removes the paper-organization paragraph, groups privacy proofs into three subsections, and adds results subheadings, a conclusion and acknowledgements. These reorganizations retain the overall narrative and most technical exposition.

P2.justification: V2 adds a two-panel frequency-coverage Figure 1. Existing Figures 1–4 become Figures 2–5, are reduced in size and relocated within the experiments section, with caption and legend adjustments. Tables 1–2 are grouped together, and algorithm displays move; existing plot trends and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through a code-access link and explicit acknowledgment of the Clueweb exception, and adds potentially useful coverage analysis. However, the new Reddit prose reports 6,340 MAD2R outputs versus 6,215 in Table 2, where 6,340 belongs to GreedyUpdate. Figure 1a's bucket totals also exceed the stated 143,556 unique items, while blanket superiority claims remain in Section 7. These unresolved reporting problems make the net quality effect uncertain.
